title: Security review - Encryption & KMS (BYOK/HSM) with Aurora Health Systems
summary: High-level security review covering encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options (BYOK/HSM), key rotation, audit logs, SOC2/HIPAA implications for healthcare data residency. Customer requested architecture diagram, SOC 2 report, and contract language around BYOK/HSM. Agreed to technical deep dive and pilot for Dedicated or Private deployment depending on network constraints.
next_steps: Samir to send SOC 2 report, security whitepaper, and BYOK architecture diagram (by 2026-04-02)
Schedule SE-led technical deep dive with Priya and Michael (week of 2026-04-06)
Provide pricing/contract language for BYOK/HSM add-on (Samir)
Customer to share network topology and compliance requirements
action_items: Samir Patel - Send SOC 2 report, security whitepaper, and BYOK/HSM architecture diagram - 2026-04-02
Emily Chen - Prepare technical deep dive deck and sample key rotation flow - 2026-04-06
Priya Singh - Share Aurora network diagram and list of required regions/data residency constraints - 2026-04-03
transcript: 00:00:00 - Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. We'll do a quick security review focused on encryption and KMS. 00:00:12 - Diane Flores: Hi Samir, Diane here, CTO at Aurora Health. Michael from security and Priya from platform are here. We run protected health info across our APIs so encryption is huge. 00:00:25 - Michael Grant: Yeah, HIPAA and state residency rules are non negotiable; want to understand BYOK, HSM, where keys live. 00:00:36 - Emily Chen: Great, I'll walk through options. Quick note: apologies for any minor audio hiss, auto-transcript may have some words off. 00:00:48 - Priya Singh: Also curious about Dedicated vs Private — network egress and peering matter for us. 00:00:58 - Samir Patel: Understood. High level: Redwood supports encryption in transit via TLS 1.2/1.3, mutual TLS option for Private, and encryption at rest via envelope encryption. We have integrations with cloud KMS and support BYOK with HSM-backed keys when requested. 00:01:20 - Michael Grant: When you say BYOK HSM, do you mean customer-managed keys in their HSM and Redwood never touches the root? 00:01:28 - Emily Chen: Correct. For BYOK + HSM we support a flow where you hold the root key in your HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3 depending on provider), and Redwood stores only wrapped data keys. We do key wrapping using your public key and we never have plaintext of your customer master key. 00:01:48 - Diane Flores: What's the process for rotation? We have quarterly rotations and strict audits. 00:01:55 - Emily Chen: We support automated rotation of data keys and you can trigger CMK rotation on your side. Typical pattern: we use envelope encryption — service-side generates DEKs (data encryption keys) per workload, those DEKs are encrypted (wrapped) by your CMK held in your KMS/HSM. Rotation is handled by issuing new DEKs and rewrapping as needed. 00:02:20 - Alex Rivera: Any limits on key sizes or algorithms? We're required to use RSA-3072 or AES-256 and prefer AES-GCM. 00:02:28 - Emily Chen: We support AES-256-GCM for data keys and AES-GCM/SHA-based AEAD for in-transit. For asymmetric operations we recommend RSA-3072 or ECDSA P-384 if you're doing signing. 00:02:44 - Michael Grant: Audit logs: we need cryptographically verifiable logs or an append-only audit with retention for 7 years for certain records. What do you provide? 00:02:55 - Liam O'Neill: Our Console provides per-request audit logs, including token-level using trace IDs, who called which model, and request headers. Logs can be exported to your SIEM (SPLUNK or GCP Stackdriver) or to an S3 bucket in your account for immutable retention. We also support forwarding to an audit HSM or WORM storage on the customer's side. 00:03:18 - Diane Flores: Is there support for immutable mode? We can't rely on Redwoods internal retention for PHI logs. 00:03:26 - Samir Patel: For Private/Dedicated deployments we normally push logs to a customer-owned bucket or your SIEM; Redwood-hosted logs are available but for compliance we recommend customer-controlled export. 00:03:40 - Priya Singh: Network-wise, do you support VPC peering and private endpoints? Latency matters for our pipelines. 00:03:47 - Emily Chen: Yes, VPC peering, private link, and on-prem connectors for air-gapped setups. In those cases you get private control plane and outbound egress policies. 00:03:59 - Michael Grant: A few specific Qs: 1) Can Redwood's engineers access plaintext in any scenario? 00:04:06 - Emily Chen: With BYOK/HSM and proper key policies, no. Engineers don't have access to your CMK. The runtime only receives wrapped DEKs; decryptions are performed using your KMS/HSM calls subject to your IAM/policy. 00:04:17 - Michael Grant: 2) Do you support HSM modules like CloudHSM, AWS Nitro, or on-prem Thales? 00:04:24 - Emily Chen: We have integrations with AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM, Azure dedicated HSM, and we can support Thales or Gemalto HSMs for on-prem via PKCS#11 bridge if you provide the network access. 00:04:38 - Diane Flores: Any certification evidence for HSM use? 00:04:42 - Emily Chen: We can share diagrams and our partner guidance; the customer HSM's FIPS level is what matters. We'll provide example policy snippets and our recommended key life-cycle docs. 00:04:55 - Alex Rivera: Data residency — we need data to remain in US-East and EU-West separately, no cross-region backups. How does Redwood handle multi-region? 00:05:05 - Liam O'Neill: We support region pinning at the tenant level. For Dedicated or Private you can restrict data to a region and we can disable cross-region failovers, though that reduces resilience; we can also provide contractual guarantees via addendum. 00:05:23 - Priya Singh: Does the model caching or KV cash use any shared storage that might cross regions? 00:05:30 - Emily Chen: Small note in the transcript: it's KV cash — meant KV cache. Our KV cache is tenant-scoped and can be pinned to region; for hosted modes there are cached layers that could be multi-region unless you opt into Dedicated/Private. 00:05:44 - Michael Grant: What's the default encryption-at-rest lifecycle for hosted vs dedicated? 00:05:50 - Emily Chen: Hosted: we use cloud-managed keys with access controls, keys rotated by Redwood unless you opt into BYOK. Dedicated/Private: default is customer-managed KMS with option for BYOK/HSM. 00:06:05 - Diane Flores: Will you accept contractual language that mandates zero-access to plaintext and restricts personnel access? 00:06:12 - Samir Patel: Yes, we typically include clauses that describe zero-access for BYOK, plus role separation and SOC 2 controls. We'll share sample contract language. 00:06:22 - Michael Grant: Key compromise scenario — what's the playbook? 00:06:26 - Emily Chen: If a CMK is suspected compromised, you can revoke access via your KMS and rotate the CMK. Because we use envelope encryption, rewrapping DEKs with a new CMK is straightforward; we can run a rewrap job if you want us to orchestrate under your control plan. We'll also provide for forensics logs; most customers trigger rotation and forensics in their HSM + shared logs. 00:06:48 - Priya Singh: Latency impact for KMS calls — we've seen external KMS calls add 50-150ms per request. How do you mitigate? 00:06:56 - Emily Chen: Good question. We cache wrapped DEKs at runtime for short TTLs to avoid synchronous KMS calls per token. For high-throughput inference we do continuous batching and keep DEKs in memory; only the initial wrap/unwarp happens with KMS, so it's amortized. For extremely low-latency workloads we recommend hosting a local KMS cluster or using dedicated peered HSM to minimize round trips. 00:07:20 - Diane Flores: For PHI we have strict logging of any key usage; can you provide per-key audit events? 00:07:27 - Liam O'Neill: Yes, we can forward KMS call metadata, but the canonical source will be your KMS logs. We cross-reference and tag requests in our trace IDs for correlation. 00:07:39 - Alex Rivera: Encryption in transit — mutual TLS supported for services-to-services? 00:07:44 - Emily Chen: Yes, mutual TLS and client certs supported in Private/Dedicated, and for hosted we support mTLS via enterprise connections. 00:07:54 - Michael Grant: SOC 2 and ISO27001 status? We need reports for procurement. 00:07:59 - Samir Patel: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified and pursuing ISO27001; we'll share the latest audit report and AOC. 00:08:08 - Alex Rivera: Any HIPAA BAAs? 00:08:11 - Samir Patel: We do offer BAA for enterprise contracts; we'll provide standard BAA language and can negotiate specific clauses with legal. 00:08:20 - Priya Singh: How are encryption keys used for embeddings and model cache? Any chance plaintext enters logs? 00:08:27 - Emily Chen: We don't log plaintext; logs include metadata and traces, not raw inputs. For embeddings and cache, inputs are encrypted at rest and in transit. If you want additional guarantees we can enable field-level encryption and redact logs for PHI. 00:08:44 - Michael Grant: Do you support per-customer KMS accounts vs shared KMS per org? 00:08:50 - Emily Chen: We support per-tenant KMS accounts and per-project key separation. For Dedicated and Private, customers generally put keys in their own KMS. 00:08:59 - Diane Flores: Are there any managed services or next steps you recommend for pilot? 00:09:05 - Samir Patel: Typically we do a small pilot in Dedicated with BYOK and route logs to your S3 + Splunk. SE can run a bench to show latency impact. 00:09:16 - Priya Singh: We'd like to do that. Also want to confirm Meltdown of human error: who can request key rotates? How granular are RBAC controls? 00:09:27 - Emily Chen: RBAC is available in Console — roles like admin, infra, auditor. Key usage can be restricted via IAM policies in your KMS; Redwood's control plane operators cannot perform KMS decrypts if BYOK enforced. 00:09:42 - Michael Grant: For long-term retention of logs and WORM requirements, can you ship to an immutable S3 bucket? 00:09:49 - Liam O'Neill: Yes, we can deliver to a WORM-enabled S3 or object-store in your cloud account. 00:09:56 - Alex Rivera: Any latency benchmarks or examples we can see? 00:10:00 - Emily Chen: We'll send a benchmark packet showing expected added latency with external KMS vs cached DEKs, and a perf run for Dedicated with peered KMS. 00:10:10 - Diane Flores: Ok, document requests: SOC 2 report, BAA draft, sample BYOK architecture, key policy snippets, and sample contract language around zero-access. 00:10:22 - Samir Patel: Noted — we'll circulate those. 00:10:26 - Michael Grant: One more security nit — HSM attestation and key import: can we import keys into CloudHSM and maintain control? 00:10:35 - Emily Chen: Yes, you can import keys to CloudHSM or use an HSM that supports key-import or external wrapping. We can accept wrapped key material per your policy. 00:10:46 - Priya Singh: For the pilot, we prefer minimal exposure — Dedicated in us-east, keys in our account, logs to our S3, run bench. 00:10:54 - Samir Patel: Sounds good. We'll scope that pilot in the next meeting. 00:10:59 - Emily Chen: Action items summary — we'll prepare technical deep dive, sample policies, and run bench. 00:11:07 - Diane Flores: Timing: we need legal review in 2 weeks, so sooner is better. 00:11:12 - Samir Patel: We'll aim to send docs within 7 business days. 00:11:18 - Alex Rivera: Quick note: transcript sometimes says Redwood product names weirdly but we know what you mean. 00:11:24 - Samir Patel: Thanks, Alex. Final recap: Samir sends docs; Emily schedules deep dive and bench; Priya shares network diagram; Michael will confirm logging/compliance checklist. 00:11:36 - Diane Flores: Thanks everyone. 00:11:39 - Samir Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up.
